title: gate add does not class a design gate push for origin/main as a ref, a gitlab/ article path or push as a plain verb
goal: bl_authority.class_reasons classes a worker's design gate design, not push, when its text names origin/main only as the ref an item file is read from, a kb article path under gitlab/, or the verb push in a sentence about screen width, while a gate about pushing to a remote stays push

run:
import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_authority as a
I={'touches':['_tools/mon_sprint.py','kb/_self/monitoring.md']}
G=[{'id':'g1','question':"Which backlog decides that a landing's item is still open?",'options':["Items of the sprint panel's backlog (origin/main item files, else the checkout's)","Item files of the checkout"]},
   {'id':'g1','question':"Where do the git fast-forward and ahead/behind facts go?",'options':['extend gitlab/git-trailers-and-hooks','new gitlab topic for git merge and status']},
   {'id':'g3','question':"How long may the needs you line get? A long list of gates would push the line far past the screen.",'options':['three entries of a kind then a count','every entry in full']}]
R=[a.class_reasons(I,g) for g in G];print(R)
sys.exit(0 if all(c!='push' for c,_ in R) else 1)

notes: SP-2uljwgho retro: three worker gates were made blocking class push by a plain word and each stopped the landing until the orchestrator answered it: BG-gkocrnfw g1 ('origin/main item files'), ST-jtbbzc6h g1 ('extend gitlab/git-trailers-and-hooks'), ST-kmgwsjto g3 ('would push the line far past the screen'). The check plants those three texts; bl_authority guards operator-only authority, so the change needs a planted push case beside each exemption (see ST-c5twwnja, ST-wxodyx66).
